stem: A grouped frequency distribution has 5 equal-width classes of width 10 each starting at 0. The frequencies are: [0-10]: f1, [10-20]: 14, [20-30]: 22, [30-40]: 10, [40-50]: f5. The total number of observations is 70 and the arithmetic mean of the distribution is 21. Find f1.

per_option_rationale.rationale: f1 = 11 arises if the student confuses the modal class midpoint (25, midpoint of [20-30]) with the distribution mean and uses 25 instead of the given value 21. With mean=25 and N=70: total fx = 1750; 5f1+45f5=640; f5=13; f1=11.
f1 = 12 arises if the student uses N = 60 (omits the [40-50] class from the total count, confusing observed and complete N). With N=60 and mean=21: total fx=1260; 5f1+45f5=150; f5=2; f1=12.

f1 = 21 arises if the student mistakenly uses the class boundary 20 as the midpoint of [10-20] rather than 15 (the class mark). With midpoints 5,20,30,40,50: known fx=14*20+22*30+10*40=280+660+400=1340; unknown=1470-1340=130; f1+f5=24; 5*(24-f5)+50*f5=130; 120-5f5+50f5=130; 45f5=10; f5=2/9 (not clean), so the student rounds and reads f1 from the boundary-based system differently, arriving near 21.

explanation: Use two simultaneous equations. Equation 1 (count): f1 + f5 = 70 - 14 - 22 - 10 = 24. Equation 2 (mean): class midpoints are 5, 15, 25, 35, 45; known sum of fx = 14*15 + 22*25 + 10*35 = 1110; so 5*f1 + 45*f5 = 21*70 - 1110 = 360. Solving: from Eq1 f5 = 24 - f1; substituting: 5*f1 + 45*(24 - f1) = 360; 1080 - 40*f1 = 360; f1 = 18.

explanation_sections.punchline: Two unknowns need two equations: total N=70 gives f1+f5=24; mean=21 gives 5*f1+45*f5=360; solving yields f1=18.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: frequency distribution with two unknown frequencies requires a simultaneous-equations approach using N and mean. Step 1: form f1+f5=24 from the total count. Step 2: form 5*f1+45*f5=21*70-1110=360 from the mean definition using class midpoints. Step 3: eliminate f5 by subtracting 5*(equation 1) from equation 2: 40*f5=240, f5=6, f1=18.
explanation_sections.lesson: When two frequencies are unknown, always form two equations: one from total count and one from the mean formula. The decisive trap is confusing class boundary with class midpoint, or using modal class midpoint instead of the given mean.
explanation_sections.timing: 150 s. Quick check: known fx = 14*15 + 22*25 + 10*35 = 210+550+350=1110; unknown fx = 1470-1110=360; standard elimination gives f5=6, f1=18.
